Hi Rhea —

Congrats on the new tutorial — onboarding is make-or-break for mobile games. If players drop out during tutorial it’s usually because the pacing or feedback isn’t matching expectations.

My approach: discovery, prototype, test. In two weeks I’ll run ten moderated sessions with players who match your target demographic, capture where they stumble, and synthesize findings into a prioritized list of fixes. I’ll include session recordings and quick-win recommendations for adjusting pacing, feedback, and UI clarity.

This will increase tutorial completion and reduce early churn by addressing the most common barriers players face. Deliverables: test plan, recordings, synthesis, and prioritized recommendations.

If this fits, let’s book a 20-minute call to finalize recruitment criteria and schedule sessions. I can start recruitment as soon as we confirm. Looking forward to your thoughts.

Warmly,
Gabi

task_instruction: Announce and invite to the monthly in-person book club meeting at the host's apartment.
task_details: Write an inviting email to the book club announcing the monthly meeting at Gabi's apartment. Include date and time (Saturday, January 17, 2026, 4:00–6:00 PM), address (Gabi's apartment in Northeast Portland — provide brief transit tip), RSVP deadline (please RSVP by Thursday, Jan 15), what to bring (a snack or drink to share), doors open time (3:50 PM for settling in), a short agenda (10-minute check-in, 40-minute discussion, closing chat and recommendations), vibe-setting line ('Low-key, bring your thoughts not a thesis'), and a friendly closing. Mention limited seating and that she’ll prep cushions and tea.
personalized:
Hey friends —

When/where: Saturday, January 17, 2026, 4:00–6:00 PM at my place in Northeast Portland (message me if you need the exact address; short Max ride or a 12-minute walk from the Hollywood stop).

Doors open at 3:50 PM so we can get comfy and pour tea (I’ll have a little corner set up with cushions).

Bring: a snack or drink to share if you’d like — nothing fancy, tienda-style bites or boba welcome. Pro tip: small plates are easiest.

Agenda: quick 10-minute check-in; 40-minute discussion of this month’s memoir pick; time to swap recs and plan the next pick.

Low-key, bring your thoughts not a thesis — this is cozy, conversational, and curiosity-forward (and yes, there will be comfy lighting). Please RSVP by Thursday, Jan 15 so I can prep seating and snacks.

If you’re coming from out of town and want to carpool, say the word — I’ll try to match people up.

Can’t wait to catch up — Gabi.

task_instruction: Invite readers to a short paid mini-workshop on mindful weekend planning
task_details: Write a newsletter inviting subscribers to a 60-minute paid mini-workshop about mindful weekend planning. Start with a reflective anecdote about intention-setting, outline what attendees will learn (three bullet-like phrases without bullets), share pricing and date, and include CTA to register.
personalized:
Have you ever reached Sunday evening and wondered where the weekend went? I used to, until I started setting two tiny intentions at the start of Saturday and saw my weekends shift from blur to meaningful pause.

In a 60-minute mini-workshop I’ll walk through a simple framework for intentional weekend planning: identify one restorative activity, choose a small project that sparks joy, and schedule a non-negotiable rest block. We’ll do a short guided reflection and leave with a flexible plan you can reuse.

The workshop is next Saturday at 10am PST, and there’s a small fee to help cover materials. Register on the blog to save your spot—space is intentionally limited to keep the conversation intimate.

With love, Gabi

Subject: Seeking Your Quick Opinion on Portfolio Aesthetics

Dear [Recipient's Name],

I'm reaching out to get your thoughts on my portfolio's visual direction. As I'm finalizing the design, I'd love to hear your opinion on which aesthetic best aligns with my goals.

I've narrowed it down to two options:

1. A minimal, neutral palette with a clean and modern look. This approach emphasizes UX rigor and clarity, making it perfect for showcasing complex design processes.
2. A warmer, "cozy" aesthetic with textured backgrounds and soft colors that nod to lifestyle content. This approach adds a personal touch while still conveying a product-first mindset.

My goal is to demonstrate clear UX rigor and signal product-first thinking while retaining an approachable personal voice. I'd love to know which aesthetic you think best achieves this balance.

Additionally, I'm considering mixing both aesthetics across different case studies. Is this a risk worth taking, or would it be better to stick to one cohesive look?

If you have a minute, I'd greatly appreciate your quick opinion on these matters. Your input will help me refine my portfolio and make a stronger impression on hiring managers and design leads.

Thank you for your time, and I look forward to hearing your thoughts.

Best,
G

Hi Jordan —

I appreciate your emphasis on inclusive design — mental health tools should be accessible to everyone (no exceptions). From our initial chat, it sounds like accessibility is on your roadmap but you need concrete evidence and developer-ready guidance before fundraising.

My approach: discovery, prototype, test. I’ll conduct a thorough accessibility audit across iOS and Android builds, combining automated scans with manual testing (keyboard navigation, screen reader flows, color contrast, touch target sizing). I’ll document each issue with annotated screenshots, severity ranking, and clear acceptance criteria that your engineers can implement and QA against.

This will reduce accessibility risk for your upcoming fundraise and lower support friction by addressing the most common barriers users currently face. Deliverables include a full audit report, prioritized remediation list, and reusable tickets that your devs can pick up immediately.

If that aligns, let’s schedule a 30-minute call to review scope and timeline. I can start the audit within a week and deliver the report in three. Looking forward to your thoughts.

Best,
Gabi

task_instruction: Send a proposal for a feature discovery workshop for a nonprofit donation funnel redesign.
task_details: Client: nonprofit focusing on community arts funding. Problem: donation funnel is long and donors drop off. Scope: half-day discovery workshop with stakeholders, mapping donor journeys, and producing a 2-week roadmap for a simplified funnel. Deliverables: workshop outputs, user journey maps, prioritized experiments, and low-fi prototypes. Budget: $2,400. Goal: reduce donation friction and increase one-time donations.
personalized:
Hi Rafael —

I love how your nonprofit centers artists; donations should be an easy outpouring, not a confusing process. A short, focused workshop can surface assumptions and align stakeholders on the fastest path to a smoother donor journey.

My approach: discovery, prototype, test. I’ll run a half-day remote workshop with your team to map donor personas and journeys, identify friction points, and define measurable experiments. After the workshop I’ll deliver user journey maps, prioritized experiments, and low-fidelity prototypes for the simplest, highest-impact changes.

This will give you a concrete two-week roadmap to reduce friction and increase one-time donations by simplifying choices and making impact clear. Deliverables include workshop artifacts, journey maps, and prototype sketches ready for dev.

If this works, let’s pick a date for the workshop and I’ll send a prep note for stakeholders. Looking forward to your thoughts — gracias.

Best,
Gabi

Subject: Request for Adoption Approval: Five New Design-System Components

Dear [Recipient],

I'm writing to request adoption approval for five new design-system components: Card, Dropdown, Toast, Datepicker, and Avatar. Each component includes comprehensive deliverables, including design tokens (spacing, color, motion), usage guidelines, and accessibility notes.

The accessibility notes for each component cover essential keyboard interactions and ARIA labels to ensure a seamless user experience. Notably, the Datepicker and Dropdown components have been thoroughly tested for keyboard navigation, and visible focus states have been added to meet the WCAG AA contrast for key elements.

Standardizing these components is expected to have a significant impact on our development workflow. It's estimated that implementing these components will reduce related screen implementation time by approximately 25% and decrease visual regressions.

If you're interested in learning more about these components, I'm happy to offer a 15-minute demo walkthrough upon request.

Please let me know if you have any questions or concerns.

Best regards,
Gabi

personalized:
In a recent usability test a user said aloud, 'Oh—that phrase made me feel seen.' Microcopy does that work: it sets tone, reduces friction, and answers hidden questions.

Three quick microcopy tips: use plain language to set expectations (avoid magical wording), use verbs for CTAs that signal value, and add small helper text where users hesitate. Pair these with short user-validated iterations and you’ll see how little copy nudges behavior.

Read the full post for before-and-after examples and downloadable snippets you can try in your next prototype.

With love, Gabi

Subject: The Power of Microcopy: Setting Tone, Reducing Friction, and Answering Hidden Questions

Dear fellow designers and product folks,

In a recent usability test, a user said aloud, "Oh—that phrase made me feel seen." Moments like these remind us of the incredible impact microcopy can have on our users' experiences. Microcopy sets tone, reduces friction, and answers hidden questions – and it's time we give it the attention it deserves.

Read the full post to learn how to harness the power of microcopy in your next prototype. We'll dive into three specific tips to get you started:

- Use plain language to set expectations (avoid magical wording).
- Use verbs for CTAs that signal value.
- Add small helper text where users hesitate.

But here's the thing: microcopy is just the beginning. To truly make a difference, pair these tips with short, user-validated iterations. Small bits of copy can nudge behavior in remarkable ways.

Want to see microcopy in action? Read the full post for before-and-after examples and downloadable snippets to try in your next project.

Best,
With love, Gabi

Subject: A Commitment to Diversity and Representation in Our Reading List

Dear [Recipient],

I am writing to acknowledge and apologize for the reading list we recently shared, which fell short of reflecting the diversity it should have. Upon reflection, I realize that a top picks list that overlooks authors of color sends the wrong message and perpetuates the lack of representation in literature.

I want to be transparent about the fact that the initial list was curated from the books I've read this year. However, I understand that this approach was narrow-minded and did not account for the rich and diverse voices that exist in literature.

To rectify this, I am committed to revising the post to include a curated section highlighting authors of color and intersectional voices. This section will be a dedicated space to celebrate the contributions of underrepresented writers and showcase the beauty of diverse perspectives.

Furthermore, I am opening the list for reader recommendations to make it richer and more representative. I invite you to reply with your favorite books, authors, and voices that you think should be included. I promise to feature and credit each recommendation that is used, giving proper recognition to the individuals who contribute to this revised list.

Your input and participation are invaluable to me, and I look forward to hearing from you. Together,

task_instruction: Send a proposal to optimize trial-to-paid messaging and CTA placements for a B2B analytics dashboard.
task_details: Client: B2B analytics dashboard for retail operations. Problem: trial users are not converting due to unclear ROI messaging. personalized:
Hi Andre —

I appreciate how data-driven your team is; the missing piece here is how trial users internalize ROI quickly. If they can’t immediately link a feature to a clear business outcome, they tend to churn.

My approach: discovery, prototype, test. Over three weeks I’ll audit existing trial messaging and CTA placement, craft a messaging framework that ties product features to retailer KPIs (e.g., inventory turn, shrink reduction), and prototype updated screens that surface ROI-driven CTAs at the point of decision.

This will increase conversions by showing value in business terms and making the next action obvious. Deliverables include a messaging framework, updated CTAs, prototype screens, and a KPI plan for measuring lift post-deploy.

If this sounds aligned, let’s schedule a quick call to review current analytics and agree on primary KPIs. I’ll share a proposed timeline and kickoff plan then. Looking forward to your thoughts.

Best,
Gabi

Hi Kira —
